title: Formed and unformed: external form for salvation-profit, not essence
source_text: XLVII. Vicissim vero Theologi Reformati non probant quod Schola Romana fidem illam mortuam & otiosam, fidem informem vocat, fidem vero formatam illam quae activa est, & per dilectionem operans; quasi charitas esset forma fidei. Sed per hoc Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae significatum volunt charitatem esse fidei formam internam & proprie dictam, quae essentiam illius absolute constituat, quod merito videtur Reformatis absurdum; sed solummodo formam quandam externam, a qua fides non habet simpliciter quod sit, sed tantum quod valeat & prosit ad salutem: in quo certe praeter locutionem ipsam, quae in se barbara est, & Scripturae inusitata, nihil est quod merito reprehendi debeat.
pass_a_gloss: Conversely the Reformed theologians do not approve that the Roman school calls that dead and idle faith unformed faith, and formed faith that which is active and working through love, as if charity were the form of faith. But by this the Doctors of the Roman Church do not mean that charity is an internal and properly so-called form of faith that absolutely constitutes its essence — which rightly seems absurd to the Reformed — but only a certain external form from which faith does not have simply that it exists, but only that it is valid and profits for salvation: in which certainly, apart from the phrasing itself, which is in itself barbarous and unused in Scripture, there is nothing that deserves to be blamed.
pass_b_english: Reformed reject informis/formata as if charity were faith inner form; Rome means only an external form that makes faith profit for salvation, not essence.
Aside from the barbarous, unscriptural phrasing, Le Blanc finds nothing else to blame in that Roman usage.

lemmas.gloss: is valid and profits for salvation

choices.why: Charity as improper external form, not essence-constituent.
rejected: charity as internal essence-form of faith
